headline: Large Energy Users Pay Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill shifts the financial burden of grid infrastructure upgrades from residential ratepayers to large energy users, primarily data centers, aiming to reduce residential utility bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, Governor Spanberger, environmental groups (Piedmont Environmental Council)
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users
news_headline: Virginia requires data centers to pay for their own power lines
news_summary: Virginia's State Corporation Commission ruled that data centers must pay the full cost for the transmission infrastructure projects they require, saving residents hundreds of millions of dollars. This decision aligns with Governor Spanberger's urging to protect Virginia families from bearing these costs.

headline: Data Center Water Use Transparency
short_summary: This bill mandates data centers to report their water consumption, providing transparency on their environmental impact and aiding state water planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups (Potomac Conservancy, Virginia League of Conservation Voters), local communities, water conservation advocates, Sen. Kannan Srinivasan
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, carried by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage, which will be aggregated and made available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to provide transparency and aid in water supply planning, especially during droughts.

headline: Local Control Data Center Siting
short_summary: This bill grants localities more authority over where data centers can be built and imposes limits on noise pollution from these facilities, requiring site assessments for high energy use facilities.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near potential data center sites, environmental groups (Virginia League of Conservation Voters)
opponents: Data center industry, economic development agencies
news_headline: P&Z starts building guardrails for data centers
news_summary: Virginia's HB 153 requires local governments to review potential impacts, including noise, before approving new data centers using 100 megawatts or more. It mandates site assessments for sound profiles on nearby homes and schools and allows localities to request reviews on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
